Table of the diagnostics for a report

Source: R/report.R
report_table.Rd

Formats the diagnostics of one analysis or of a comparison as a table in the layout of Table 5 of Lee (2026): the informativeness, the mean reliability and the dispersion with their posterior intervals, the concentration count and the posterior probability that the informativeness exceeds the threshold.

Usage

report_table(x, digits = 2, format = c("data.frame", "markdown", "latex"))

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_posterior, reliability_draws, reliability_profile or profile_comparison.

digits

Number of decimals of the informativeness, the mean reliability and the probability, a positive integer; the dispersion has one more and the concentration count 1.

format

"data.frame" (the default) for a data frame of numbers, "markdown" or "latex" for text in the style of the paper.

Value

For format = "data.frame", a data frame with one row per analysis and the columns analysis, J, I, I_lower, I_upper, mean, H, H_lower, H_upper, J_eff and prob_I_above, and the note in its attribute note. For the text formats, a character string.

Details

In the text formats the leading zeros of the numbers between 0 and 1 are dropped and intervals are in brackets, as in the paper. A table of one analysis has no column for its name; the names of a comparison label its rows. The LaTeX table uses the rules of the booktabs package. Every format ends with a note that states the working model, the prior, the scale and the estimand when the fits record them, the conditioning on the standard errors, and that each site counts equally in the diagnostics.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, data = eight_schools)
report_table(fit)
#>   analysis J         I      I_lower   I_upper      mean          H      H_lower
#> 1 analysis 8 0.2252945 0.0003997828 0.7451728 0.2297284 0.01428773 4.407725e-05
#>      H_upper    J_eff prob_I_above
#> 1 0.02832835 7.170045    0.1379141
cat(report_table(fit, format = "markdown"))
#> | J | I [95% interval] | Mean reliability | H [95% interval] | J_eff | Pr(I > 0.5) |
#> |:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
#> | 8 | .23 [.00, .75] | .23 | .014 [.000, .028] | 7.2 | .14 |
#> 
#> *Note.* Each estimate is modeled as normal around its site's effect with a known sampling variance, and the site effects as independent and normal across sites. Flat priors on the mean and the between-site standard deviation. Summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors, and each site counts equally in the diagnostics, whatever its size.
